sections.title: Volume, Take Rate & Net Revenue
sections.subtitle: The core engine: net revenue = processed volume × take rate. Q1/Q3 business-update rows are revenue-only snapshots that overlap the half-years and are excluded from every chart below to avoid double-counting.

charts.title: Take Rate
charts.annotation: 22.3bps (H1 2018) fell to a 14.7bps trough (H1 2024), then recovered to 17.1bps (H2 2025) before easing to 16.2bps (H1 2026). Management calls this volume tiering, not price competition -- the single most-watched line on this dashboard.

charts.title: Net Revenue / Volume Cross-Check

netRevenue.title: Net Revenue
netRevenue.content:
Net revenue is Adyen's top line: the take-rate and fixed fees it earns on processed volume, net of interchange and scheme fees passed through to card networks and issuing banks. This is deliberately different from the generic Revenue field (blank for Adyen by design) because Adyen itself reports net revenue as the headline metric.

For Adyen: €1,302.9m in H1 2026, +19.1% reported / +21% constant currency, split Digital €719.7m (+13%), Unified Commerce €417.7m (+25%) and Platforms €165.5m (+37%, now ~13% of the total and the fastest-growing pillar).

What to watch:

  • Digital pillar growth durability after recovering from Q1 2026's record-low +9%/+13% CC print
  • FY2026 guidance was raised to 21-23% CC, including ~1pp from the July 2026 Talon.One/Orb acquisitions

processedVolume.title: Processed Volume
processedVolume.content:
Processed volume is the total value of payments Adyen processes for merchants (reported in EUR billions, not millions — note the different scale from every other chart on this page). Net revenue is a small percentage of this figure (the take rate).

For Adyen: €803.8bn in H1 2026, +24% YoY, driven by Platforms (+42%) and Unified Commerce (+27%) outgrowing Digital (+17%).

What to watch:

  • Volume consistently growing faster than net revenue is the visible signature of take-rate compression — management's explanation is deliberate volume tiering, not competitive discounting

takeRate.title: Take Rate
takeRate.content:
Take rate is net revenue divided by processed volume, expressed in basis points (bps). It is the single most important number on this dashboard: Adyen's entire growth story is volume compounding at a high rate while take rate erodes gently as large customers scale and negotiate better unit pricing.

For Adyen: 22.3bps at IPO (H1 2018) declined to a 14.7bps trough (H1 2024), recovered to 17.1bps (H2 2025), and eased to 16.2bps in H1 2026. Management frames the H1 2026 dip as expected 'volume tiering' rather than competitive pricing pressure, citing that volume (+24%) grew faster than net revenue (+21% CC) by a modest, not alarming, gap, and that customer concentration is improving (top 300 customers now ~60% of growth, down from over 70% three years ago).

What to watch:

  • Whether take rate stabilizes near/above 16bps over the next 1-2 halves — the DCF's base case treats the decline as mostly benign but still decelerates growth slightly faster than volume through the decade (20% down to 7.5%) rather than fully trusting management's framing, because it cannot yet be independently verified against competitive discounting; the bear case takes the opposite view outright, with growth collapsing to 11% by year 2
  • This is the first item in the DCF's own key-metrics-to-watch list

takeRateCheck.title: Net Revenue / Volume Cross-Check
takeRateCheck.content:
A derived sanity check: NetRevenue ÷ ProcessedVolume, expressed in bps, plotted against the reported TakeRate column. The two should track closely since take rate is defined as this ratio.

For Adyen: used here purely as a data-quality check, not as an independent metric — a widening gap between the two lines would signal a change in how Adyen defines or nets volume/revenue, which is worth investigating before trusting either in isolation.

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin
ebitdaMargin.content:
EBITDA margin is reported EBITDA divided by net revenue. Adyen's IFRS operating expenses already include stock-based compensation, so this is a post-SBC margin (no separate SBC add-back needed to compare across periods).

For Adyen: dipped to 43.3% in H1 2023 during a deliberate hiring cycle, recovered to 55.0% by H2 2025, then eased to 49.2% in H1 2026 (50% excluding one-off Talon.One/Orb transaction costs) on acquisition dilution and continued investment. H2 is seasonally stronger than H1 by 4-6pp every year since 2023 — do not read an H1-to-H2 change as trend.

What to watch:

  • Management's long-term target is above 55% by 2028; FY2026 guidance is for underlying margin roughly in line with 2025 but ~1pp lower including the acquisitions

fcf.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Compares reported net income against reported free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex) as recorded in the Metrics CSV.

For Adyen: FCF of €553.4m in H1 2026 (+17% YoY) represents 86% EBITDA conversion — a high-quality cash business with modest working-capital drag.

What to watch:

  • Full-year 2026 capex guidance was raised sharply to 7% of net revenue (from ‘up to 5%’) to pull forward 2027 datacenter spend; H1 2026 capex ran at only 5% of net revenue, implying a much sharper H2 step-up that could compress FCF conversion in the second half

ownerFcf.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF (TTM)
ownerFcf.content:
Owner FCF, as used in the DCF, strips finance income Adyen earns on its own cash from reported free cash flow. That interest income is a rate-cycle windfall on the cash balance (it rose from €29.3m in FY2022 to €246-350m in FY2023-25 as policy rates rose), and the underlying cash is separately added back as a balance-sheet asset in the DCF bridge — counting the interest AND the cash pile would double-count the same asset.

For Adyen: TTM reported FCF of €1,160.2m vs TTM owner FCF of €888.1m to 30-Jun-2026 — a gap of roughly €272m, almost entirely the finance-income strip rather than SBC (which is genuinely small at 1.85% of net revenue).

This chart shows a single TTM snapshot from the DCF JSON, not a period-by-period CSV series — owner FCF is not tracked historically period-by-period in the source data.

Why the valuation moved: this DCF replaces a 9-Aug-2026 run whose weighted intrinsic value was €769.52. The single largest correction (+€305) was lengthening the horizon from 5 to 10 years — the year-5 owner-FCF margin was still climbing, so a 5-year build capitalized an immature margin in perpetuity. Smaller moves: restoring house-default 15/50/35 weights from a temporary 25/50/25 (+€63) after the H1 print resolved the uncertainty that justified the extra bear weight; a single 10.5% WACC replacing scenario-varying rates (−€38, since risk is now charged once, in the flows); and rolling the revenue base forward to TTM and the FY2026 guidance raise (+€63 combined). See the DCF JSON’s own reconciliation field for the full line-by-line bridge.

Sanity check is one-directional by design: Adyen has de-rated on every multiple (P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, P/S) every year since its 2018 IPO, when multiples were hypergrowth-era artifacts, not re-rating targets. The DCF’s sanity check can fail a model whose implied multiples sit ABOVE historical norms, but the fact that today’s multiples (P/E 30.3, P/B 6.45, EV/EBITDA 20.8) sit below every historical year is NOT evidence the stock is cheap — no part of this valuation rests on that comparison. The DCF stands on projected cash flows alone.

headlineCash.title: Headline Cash vs Merchant Payables
headlineCash.content:
Adyen's balance-sheet CashAndEquivalents is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float that Adyen holds briefly between collecting from a card scheme and paying out to the merchant — it is not Adyen's money. The offsetting liability, PayablesToMerchants, shows how much of that cash is owed straight back out.

For Adyen: at 30-Jun-2026, headline cash was €12,392.8m against payables to merchants of €8,097.4m. Netting payables and adding receivables from merchants/financial institutions of €602.8m gives Adyen's own cash of €4,898.2m — which ties to the H1 2026 letter's own statement that ‘our cash stood at €4.9 billion’. Net of the July 2026 Talon.One and Orb acquisitions, management stated this would be approximately €4.6 billion; the DCF uses €4,190m as its net-cash bridge input.

Never read the €12.4bn headline as a cash pile or a net-cash figure — it is the single most misleading number on this balance sheet if taken at face value.

revPerFte.title: Net Revenue per FTE
revPerFte.content:
A derived efficiency metric: net revenue divided by full-time-equivalent headcount. Rising revenue per FTE indicates the platform is scaling faster than the organization needed to run it.

For Adyen: FTE reached 5,020 at H1 2026. Adyen has historically grown revenue per FTE over time, though the pace varies with deliberate hiring cycles (e.g. the 2023 investment push that compressed EBITDA margin).

FTE is only disclosed at select half-year points in the source filings; periods without a figure are simply omitted from this line rather than interpolated.

sbcShares.title: Stock-Based Compensation & Shares Outstanding
sbcShares.content:
Tracks reported SBC expense alongside diluted shares outstanding.

For Adyen: SBC is genuinely small at roughly 1.85% of net revenue (TTM to H1 2026), far below the 10-15% typical of US tech comparables. Adyen conducts zero buybacks and pays zero dividends — 100% earnings retention — so shares outstanding have drifted up only modestly (30.5m FY2020 to 31.567m at Jun-2026, ~0.65%/year) despite continuous SBC issuance. The DCF holds the share count flat across its 10-year forecast on the view that SBC is already fully expensed inside reported EBITDA, so compounding the share count as well would charge grant dilution twice.

Capital allocation / M&A judgement call: the July 2026 Talon.One and Orb acquisitions (~€1.05bn combined) mark Adyen’s first-ever purchases after eight years of 100% organic growth. The bull case credits further disciplined deployment and a slower growth decay (10.5% still in year 10 vs 7.5% base); the bear case treats the ~1pp of 2026 growth bought for ~€1.05bn as a poor initial return and charges integration risk through a stalled 52.7% terminal margin, short of the 55% 2028 target. Balance-sheet treatment is symmetric across scenarios.

Governance: the CFO departure (effective 31-Aug-2026, interim Hwa Tsao), Co-CEO Pieter van der Does’s health-related step-back and return, a new CPO and APAC succession represent unusually concentrated turnover for a founder-culture company. This is charged through the bear case’s execution assumptions and its 15% probability weight, deliberately NOT through a WACC premium — charging it in the discount rate as well would count the same risk twice.

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, before finance income on own cash
